title: Trading Sessions & Market Hours
hook: Different sessions, different behavior. Know which one you're looking at.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to weigh a chart move differently depending on which session it formed in.

blocks.heading: The same chart behaves differently depending on what time it is

beats.heading: Three sessions, three personalities
beats.body: Asia tends to be quiet and range-bound. London often brings the first real expansion. New York — especially the RTH open — usually brings the highest volume and sharpest moves.

beats.heading: Not "better," just different
beats.body: None of this means one session is better. It means the same setup can look completely different depending on which session it's forming in.

blocks.heading: Weigh the test
sequence: A level gets tested overnight on thin volume
blocks.askAfter: A level gets tested overnight on thin volume
blocks.prompt: That same level gets retested at the New York open with much higher volume. Which test carries more information?

options.label: The New York open retest — more participation, more real signal
options.feedback: Right — more real participants means the reaction reflects more genuine agreement or disagreement.

options.label: They're equal
options.feedback: Volume differences between sessions are real information, not noise to ignore.

blocks.quote: I'm not telling you to only trade one session. I'm telling you to know which session you're looking at, because a level in London and a level at the New York open don't carry the same weight.

questions.question: A trader sees a clean-looking break of structure during the thin overnight session, then the exact same level gets retested with much higher volume at the New York open. Which read should she trust more?
options: The New York retest — higher volume and participation make the reaction more meaningful
They're identical — session doesn't change how a break should be read
The overnight break is more reliable because it happened first
questions.why: More volume and participation means the reaction reflects more real conviction.

questions.question: The New York session (RTH open) typically brings the highest ___ and sharpest moves.
questions.why: It overlaps with US stock market hours and major news, driving the most participation.

takeaways: Asia, London, and New York each behave differently — none is "better," just different.
A move on heavy volume carries more real information than the same-looking move on thin volume.
Ignoring session context throws away free, useful information.
remember: A level in London and a level at the New York open don't carry the same weight.
